findings.who: A participant in an employee stock ownership plan (ESOP) whose employer paid dividends directly to them in 2025; the shares are held inside the ESOP, a retirement account, and the 2025 Form 1099-DIV arrives in 2026.
findings.why_no: They answer no because they did not own shares outside a retirement account and did not get a Form 1099-DIV during calendar 2025.
findings.irs_text: f1099div p. 5, Box 1b: 'The amount shown may be dividends a corporation paid directly to you as a participant (or beneficiary of a participant) in an employee stock ownership plan (ESOP). Report it as a dividend on your Form 1040 or 1040-SR...'
findings.fix: Ask about dividends or a 2025 Form 1099-DIV received in 2025 or 2026, including ESOP dividends paid directly to a participant, even when the shares are inside a retirement account.

findings.who: A nominee recipient who receives a 2025 Form 1099-DIV in 2026 showing ordinary dividends that belong to another person; they own no shares in 2025.
findings.why_no: They answer no because in 2025 they neither owned shares nor got the form; the form arrived in 2026.
findings.irs_text: i1040sb p. 2, Line 5, Nominees: 'If you received a Form 1099-DIV that includes ordinary dividends you received as a nominee (that is, in your name, but the ordinary dividends actually belong to someone else), report the total on line 5.'
findings.fix: Ask about a 2025 Form 1099-DIV received in 2025 or 2026 and explicitly cover nominee amounts and amounts belonging to another.

findings.who: A filer who sold all shares in December 2024 but received an ordinary dividend in January 2025 because they were the holder of record; they owned no shares in 2025 and the 2025 Form 1099-DIV arrives in 2026.
findings.why_no: They answer no because 'In 2025' they did not own shares and did not get a Form 1099-DIV in 2025.
findings.irs_text: i1040sb p. 2, Line 5: 'Report on line 5 all of your ordinary dividends. This amount should be shown in box 1a of your Forms 1099-DIV or substitute statements.'
findings.fix: Gate on receiving any ordinary dividend for 2025, including a dividend paid in 2025 on shares sold before 2025.

findings.who: A filer whose company or fund closed or whose shares were canceled before 2025, but who receives a final return-of-capital or liquidation distribution in 2025 without a Form 1099-DIV.
findings.why_no: They answer no because they did not own shares in 2025 and got no Form 1099-DIV; the gated question's help says to count a no-form return of capital or a payout when a company closed.
findings.irs_text: f1099div p. 5, Box 3: 'Shows a return of capital... Any amount received in excess of your basis is taxable to you as capital gain'; Boxes 9 and 10: 'Show cash and noncash liquidation distributions.'
findings.fix: Gate on receiving any 2025 distribution, including a no-form return of capital or liquidation distribution, even if the shares were no longer held in 2025.

findings.who: A REIT shareholder who receives a Form 2439 for 2025 but no Form 1099-DIV because the REIT retained the gains; they do not see REITs in the gate's help list of stocks, mutual funds, ETFs and money market funds.
findings.why_no: They answer no because they did not get a 1099-DIV and do not think a REIT is a 'company or fund' from the examples.
findings.irs_text: i1040sd p. 6: 'Include on Schedule D, line 11, the amount from box 1a of Form 2439. This represents your share of the undistributed long-term capital gains of the regulated investment company (including a mutual fund) or real estate investment trust.'
findings.fix: Add REITs and other RICs to the gate help, or ask directly whether any Form 2439 was received.

findings.who: A beneficial owner of municipal-fund shares held in another person's name who receives exempt-interest dividends in 2025 without a Form 1099-DIV; they do not own shares in their own name.
findings.why_no: They answer no because they did not own shares in their own name and did not get a Form 1099-DIV.
findings.irs_text: f1099div p. 5, Box 12: 'Shows exempt-interest dividends from a mutual fund or other RIC paid to you during the calendar year'; i1040sb p. 2: 'Also include on line 2a ... any exempt-interest dividends from a mutual fund or other regulated investment company.'
findings.fix: Ask about exempt-interest dividends received for 2025, directly or through another name and with or without a form.

findings.who: A beneficial owner of shares held in another person's name who receives ordinary dividends in 2025 without a Form 1099-DIV; they do not own shares in their own name.
findings.why_no: They answer no because they did not own shares in their own name and did not get a Form 1099-DIV.
findings.irs_text: i1040sb p. 2, Line 5: 'Report on line 5 all of your ordinary dividends...' and the Nominees paragraph for Form 1099-DIV amounts belonging to another.
findings.fix: Ask whether they received any ordinary dividends for 2025, directly or through someone else, with or without a form.

findings.who: A beneficial owner of fund shares held in another person's name who receives a capital gain distribution in 2025 without a Form 1099-DIV.
findings.why_no: They answer no because they did not own shares in their own name and did not get a Form 1099-DIV.
findings.irs_text: f1099div p. 5, Box 2a: 'Shows total capital gain distributions from a regulated investment company (RIC) or real estate investment trust (REIT).'
findings.fix: Ask whether they received any capital gain distribution for 2025, with or without a form and including amounts paid through another name.

findings.who: A filer received capital gain distributions from a mutual fund or REIT but got no Form 1099-DIV. For example, the form never arrived, was lost, or the fund sent only a year-end statement that designates part of the distribution as unrecaptured section 1250 gain or 28% collectibles gain. The tool takes the box 2a amount as an amount received without a form.
findings.why_no: The gate asks whether there is 'An amount in box 2b, 2c, 2d, 2e, 2f, 3, 9, 10 or 13 of any Form 1099-DIV'. The filer has no Form 1099-DIV, so 'no' is a truthful answer. The gated questions' own help says to include 'any amount received without a form', but the filer never sees that help.
findings.irs_text: f1099div p. 5: 'Box 2b. Shows the portion of the amount in box 2a that is unrecaptured section 1250 gain from certain depreciable real property'; 'Box 2d. Shows the portion of the amount in box 2a that is 28% rate gain from sales or exchanges of collectibles'
findings.fix: Ask about the fact, not the form: 'Did any part of your or your spouse's capital gain distributions consist of unrecaptured section 1250 gain, section 1202 gain, collectibles (28%) gain, or section 897 gain, as shown on a Form 1099-DIV or a fund or REIT statement, or as received without a form?'

findings.who: A filer owns fund or REIT shares that are held in someone else's name, so the Form 1099-DIV goes to that person. Examples: a parent or co-owner is the named recipient, or a nominee holds the shares. That form shows an amount in box 2b or 2d, and the filer's share of it is the filer's own income.
findings.why_no: The filer reads 'any Form 1099-DIV' as forms issued to them or their spouse. None of those forms shows these boxes, so the filer answers no. The gated help says to 'Include your share of amounts paid in someone else's name', but that help is shown only after a yes.
findings.irs_text: f1099div p. 5, Nominees: 'If this form includes amounts belonging to another person, you are considered a nominee recipient. You must file Form 1099-DIV ... for each of the other owners to show their share of the income'
findings.fix: Move the nominee and no-form instructions into the gate: '...on any Form 1099-DIV issued to you, your spouse, or another person for shares you own, or received without a form'.

findings.who: A filer answers using the original Form 1099-DIV, which shows only box 2a. The fund later issues a CORRECTED Form 1099-DIV that reclassifies part of box 2a into box 2b or box 2d. Funds often reallocate distributions after year end.
findings.why_no: The filer answers from the first form they received. They do not think to re-check for a corrected form.
findings.irs_text: f1099div p. 4: 'CORRECTED (if checked)'; p. 5: 'Box 2b. Shows the portion of the amount in box 2a that is unrecaptured section 1250 gain'
findings.fix: Add to the gate's help: 'Use the latest form, including any CORRECTED Form 1099-DIV.'

findings.who: A filer whose consolidated brokerage statement shows box 2a, with box 2b or 2d amounts listed below it as part of that total.
findings.why_no: Boxes 2b–2d are 'the portion of the amount in box 2a'. The filer may think the 2a total already covers these amounts and that reporting them again would double count, so they answer no. A consolidated statement may also show descriptive labels without box numbers, so the filer cannot match the gate's box numbers.
findings.irs_text: f1099div p. 5: 'Box 2a ... But, if no amount is shown in boxes 2b, 2c, 2d, and 2f and your only capital gains and losses are capital gain distributions, you may be able to report the amounts shown in box 2a on your Form 1040'
findings.fix: Name each box by its label as well as its number ('Unrecap. Sec. 1250 gain', 'Section 1202 gain', 'Collectibles (28%) gain', 'Section 897 capital gain'). State that these are portions of box 2a and are still needed even though box 2a is already entered.

findings.who: A nonresident or dual-status individual filing a U.S. return whose Form 1099-DIV shows an amount only in box 2f.
findings.why_no: The filer may read the gate's 'less common boxes' as boxes that do not apply to them. The Note on boxes 2e and 2f does say they apply to foreign persons, but a filer who does not see themselves as a 'foreign person or entity' may answer no.
findings.irs_text: f1099div p. 5: 'Box 2f. Shows the portion of the amount in box 2a that is section 897 gain attributable to disposition of USRPI. Note: Boxes 2e and 2f apply only to foreign persons and entities ... generally treated as effectively connected'
findings.fix: Say: 'Answer yes if any of these boxes shows any amount, even if you think it does not apply to you.'

findings.who: A parent who elects to include a child’s dividends on the parent’s return on Form 8814, where neither the parent nor spouse has any Form 1099-DIV box 1a ordinary dividends but the child has box 1b qualified dividends.
findings.why_no: The gate is computed from 'Total ordinary dividends, Form 1099-DIV box 1a, when you or your spouse received dividends'; the parent truthfully says no because the dividends were the child’s, not the parent’s or spouse’s.
findings.irs_text: i1040gi p. 25, Line 3a: "If you are including your child’s qualified dividends in the total on line 3a, check box 1 on line 3c."
findings.fix: Broaden the gate to include a child’s ordinary and qualified dividends included through Form 8814, and ask separately for the child’s box 1b amount on line 3a.

findings.who: A filer whose only qualified dividends are not reported on Form 1099-DIV—for example, qualified dividends passed through on a partnership or S-corporation Schedule K-1, received from a foreign payer, or paid by a payer that issued no Form 1099-DIV—and who therefore has no Form 1099-DIV box 1a amount.
findings.why_no: The gate is worded as 'Ordinary dividends (box 1a) are above zero' and is computed from Form 1099-DIV box 1a; with no such box 1a amount the filer truthfully answers no, even though the non-1099-DIV qualified dividends belong on line 3a.
findings.irs_text: i1040gi p. 25, Line 3a: "See Pub. 550 for the definition of qualified dividends if you received dividends not reported on Form 1099-DIV."
findings.fix: Gate line 3a on qualified dividends themselves, including non-1099-DIV qualified dividends, or broaden the gate to any dividends and then ask separately for box 1a, box 1b, and non-1099-DIV qualified dividends.

findings.who: A filer whose Form 1099-DIV shows qualified dividends in box 1b but who reads 'ordinary dividends' as excluding 'qualified dividends' and therefore treats box 1a as zero or answers no.
findings.why_no: The gate says 'Ordinary dividends (box 1a) are above zero'; the filer thinks qualified dividends are a separate category, not part of ordinary dividends, despite box 1b being a portion of box 1a.
findings.irs_text: i1040gi p. 25, Line 3a: "Qualified dividends are also included in the ordinary dividend total required to be shown on line 3b."
findings.fix: State in the gate that box 1a includes box 1b qualified dividends, or gate line 3a on qualified dividends rather than on ordinary dividends.

findings.who: A filer whose Form 1099-DIV shows section 199A dividends in box 5 but who reads 'ordinary dividends' as excluding section 199A dividends and therefore treats box 1a as zero or answers no.
findings.why_no: The gate says 'Ordinary dividends (box 1a) are above zero'; the filer sees box 5 as a separate 'section 199A dividends' amount and does not realize box 5 is a portion of box 1a.
findings.irs_text: f1099div p. 5, Instructions for Recipient: "Box 5. Shows the portion of the amount in box 1a that may be eligible for the 20% qualified business income deduction under section 199A."
findings.fix: State in the gate that box 1a includes box 5 section 199A dividends, or gate the box 5 question directly on whether box 5 is present.

findings.who: A filer whose Form 1099-DIV (or a spouse's, on a joint return) shows an amount in box 3. The filer, or both spouses, do not treat box 3 as one of the 'less common boxes'.
findings.why_no: The box 3 amount reaches the gate only through the parent helper, 'when a Form 1099-DIV shows an amount in one of the less common boxes.' A filer who sees boxes 1a, 1b, 2a and 3 on most fund statements, or who reads a list of 'less common' boxes as complete, answers no to the parent. Box 3 then stays zero and the gate is false.
findings.irs_text: f1099div p. 5, Box 3: 'Shows a return of capital... Any amount received in excess of your basis is taxable to you as capital gain.'
findings.fix: Ask about box 3 directly for every Form 1099-DIV entered, and do not route it through a 'less common boxes' parent. Ask: 'Does box 3 (Nondividend distributions) on any Form 1099-DIV for you or your spouse show an amount above zero?'

findings.who: A filer holding a closed-end fund, REIT or other stock that paid a return of capital in 2025. Earlier returns of capital have already reduced the basis to zero.
findings.why_no: Box 3 is described as 'not taxable', so the filer sees no reason to report a nontaxable amount and leaves it out or answers no to the less-common-boxes parent. The help text does not say that box 3 can be taxable when it exceeds the remaining basis.
findings.irs_text: f1099div p. 5, Box 3: 'To the extent of your cost (or other basis) in the stock, the distribution reduces your basis and is not taxable. Any amount received in excess of your basis is taxable to you as capital gain.'
findings.fix: In the help for the box 3 entry or the parent question, say: 'Enter box 3 even though it is often not taxable. It becomes taxable once it exceeds your remaining basis in the shares.'

findings.who: A filer or spouse who received a nondividend distribution (a return of capital in excess of the corporation's earnings) without a Form 1099-DIV. Examples are a payer that did not issue the form, a foreign corporation, or a closely held C corporation. Earlier distributions had already reduced the basis to zero.
findings.why_no: The gate is computed only from box 3 of a Form 1099-DIV. With no form there is truthfully no box 3 amount, so the gate is false and the basis question is never asked. The part above basis is a capital gain whether or not a form was issued, and the tool should refuse to complete the return.
findings.irs_text: f1099div p. 5, Box 3: 'Shows a return of capital... Any amount received in excess of your basis is taxable to you as capital gain. See Pub. 550.'
findings.fix: Add a broad gate question: 'Did you or your spouse receive in 2025 any distribution that the payer described as a return of capital or nondividend distribution, whether or not it was reported in box 3 of a Form 1099-DIV?' Ask the basis question on a yes, or refuse when no amount is supplied.

findings.who: A filer whose section 897 ordinary dividend is not on any Form 1099-DIV. Examples are a dual-status or treaty filer paid by a U.S. REIT or RIC and reported on Form 1042-S, and a filer whose payer sent no form at all.
findings.why_no: The gate asks about 'An amount in box 2b, 2c, 2d, 2e ... of any Form 1099-DIV'. No Form 1099-DIV shows the amount, so the no is truthful. Yet the gated question's help says to include 'any amount received without a form', and the filer never sees that help.
findings.irs_text: f1099div p. 5: 'Box 2e. Shows the portion of the amount in box 1a that is section 897 gain attributable to disposition of U.S. real property interests (USRPI).'
findings.fix: Match the gate to the help: 'Did any of your or your spouse's dividends include amounts of these kinds (box 2b–2f, 3, 9, 10 or 13 of a Form 1099-DIV, or the same amounts on another statement or with no form)?'

findings.who: A joint filer with a share of a section 897 dividend from a jointly held or nominee account. The Form 1099-DIV is issued in a parent's, sibling's or co-owner's name and shows the amount in box 2e.
findings.why_no: The gate says 'of any Form 1099-DIV, when you or your spouse owned shares or received a Form 1099-DIV'. The filer reads 'any Form 1099-DIV' as forms they or their spouse received. Their own forms show nothing in the listed boxes, so they answer no, although the help says 'Include your share of amounts paid in someone else's name.'
findings.irs_text: f1099div p. 5: 'Nominees. If this form includes amounts belonging to another person, you are considered a nominee recipient.' and 'Box 2e. Shows the portion of the amount in box 1a that is section 897 gain...'
findings.fix: Add to the gate: 'including your share of a form issued in someone else's name (a nominee or joint account)'.

findings.who: A filer whose broker sends a consolidated substitute statement. On it, section 897 ordinary dividends appear as a labeled line, sometimes on a supplemental page, without the '2e' box number.
findings.why_no: The gate lists bare box numbers ('box 2b, 2c, 2d, 2e ...'), and the line's own label calls these 'the less common boxes'. The filer does not match the labeled line to '2e' and answers no.
findings.irs_text: f1099div p. 2: box '2e Section 897 ordinary dividends'
findings.fix: Give each box's printed caption next to its number in the gate, e.g. '2e Section 897 ordinary dividends', and add 'on Form 1099-DIV or a broker's substitute statement'.

findings.who: A shareholder of a closely held or foreign corporation that paid a return of capital or a cash or property liquidating distribution in 2025. The company issued no Form 1099-DIV, which is common for small private companies and usual for foreign corporations.
findings.why_no: They can answer yes to the ownership question. The computed condition then asks for 'An amount in box 2b, 2c, 2d, 2e, 2f, 3, 9, 10 or 13 of any Form 1099-DIV', and with no form they truthfully answer no. The gated help says 'any amount received without a form' counts, but that help appears only after the gate is passed.
findings.irs_text: f1099div p. 5: 'Box 3. Shows a return of capital ... Any amount received in excess of your basis is taxable to you as capital gain'; 'Boxes 9 and 10. Show cash and noncash liquidation distributions.'
findings.fix: Ask about the fact, with or without a form: 'In 2025, did you or your spouse receive a return of capital, nondividend distribution, or liquidating distribution (cash or property) from a company or fund, or a Form 1099-DIV with an amount in box 2b–2f, 3, 9, 10 or 13?'

findings.who: A shareholder whose company liquidated, or was acquired with a holdback or escrow, so the shares were cancelled in 2024. A final liquidating payment arrived in 2025, but the 2025 Form 1099-DIV was not issued, was lost, or comes in 2026 after the filer considers the matter closed.
findings.why_no: 'In 2025, did you ... own shares' is no because the shares were gone before 2025. 'Or get a Form 1099-DIV' reads as a form arriving during 2025, and a form for 2025 arrives in 2026. They answer no.
findings.irs_text: f1099div p. 5: 'Boxes 9 and 10. Show cash and noncash liquidation distributions.'
findings.fix: Add: 'or receive any payment or property in 2025 from a company or fund whose shares you or your spouse own now or owned earlier (including a final liquidating payment), or get a Form 1099-DIV for 2025.'

findings.who: A holder of interests that the filer does not think of as 'shares of a company or a fund', such as liquidating-trust units, unit investment trust units, or non-traded REIT or interval fund units. These pay nondividend distributions or liquidation distributions.
findings.why_no: The filer reads 'shares of a company or a fund' as stock or mutual fund shares and does not count 'units' or 'beneficial interests'. If the payer's statement is a composite or year-end letter rather than a separate Form 1099-DIV, they also answer no to 'get a Form 1099-DIV'.
findings.irs_text: f1099div p. 5: 'Box 3. Shows a return of capital. To the extent of your cost (or other basis) in the stock, the distribution reduces your basis'; 'Box 2a. ... from a regulated investment company (RIC) or real estate investment trust (REIT).'
findings.fix: Broaden the gate to 'shares, units, or other interests in a company, fund, REIT, trust, or similar investment' and mention year-end or composite tax statements from a broker or fund.

findings.who: A spouse on a joint return whose return-of-capital or AMT municipal fund dividends were reported to the other spouse, or a filer with a share of a joint or nominee account that was reported in another person's name.
findings.why_no: The second question, 'An amount in box ... of any Form 1099-DIV', does not repeat 'you or your spouse' and does not mention forms issued in someone else's name. A filer may check only their own forms.
findings.irs_text: f1099div p. 5: 'Box 13. Shows exempt-interest dividends subject to the alternative minimum tax. This amount is included in box 12.'; 'If this form includes amounts belonging to another person, you are considered a nominee recipient.'
findings.fix: Word the condition as 'On any Form 1099-DIV for you, your spouse, or an account in someone else's name in which you have a share, is there an amount in box 2b, 2c, 2d, 2e, 2f, 3, 9, 10 or 13?'
